interpretation: Projected attack paths: not confirmed attacks, and not a likelihood assessment. An LLM placed techniques that MITRE ATT&CK documents this actor using onto the organization's own flow map, reasoning the way an adversary would. Technique ids, technique names and controls are sourced; the route, the step rationales and the access states are the model's projection. Each step's access is checked only for continuity — that an earlier step produced what the step needs — never for truth. A step that states no access falls back to a typical value for its tactic.

attack_sequence.name: Spearphishing Link on End users (internet, outside the network)
attack_sequence.description: End users accessing the SPA are targeted with malicious links to harvest their primary Okta credentials.
success_indicators: Attacker acquires valid Okta username and password.
attack_sequence.precondition: Attacker has established infrastructure to host a credential harvesting page masquerading as the application's login.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Human susceptibility to social engineering combined with the external internet exposure of the end user demographic.
assumptions: Users can be identified via OSINT
Harvesting infrastructure is not blocked by threat intelligence feeds
attack_sequence.control_note: Bypasses technical perimeter controls by targeting the human element outside the managed network.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: APT29 has used spearphishing with a link to trick victims into clicking on a link to a zip file containing malicious files.

attack_sequence.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation on Okta
attack_sequence.description: APT29 uses MFA fatigue to push repeated authentication requests to the user's device until they approve it, bypassing Okta's primary access policies.
detecting_controls: Okta sign-on and access policies
Token lifetime and audience validation
success_indicators: Attacker establishes a fully authenticated Okta session and extracts the OAuth2 OIDC bearer token.
attack_sequence.precondition: Attacker possesses the user's valid primary Okta credentials.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The identity provider relies on push notifications or user-approved MFA prompts which can be flooded.
assumptions: MFA rate limiting is insufficient to stop prompt bombing
User eventually approves the request out of frustration or confusion
attack_sequence.control_note: Subverts Okta MFA access policies by relying on user authorization fatigue rather than technical cryptographic bypass.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: APT29 has used repeated MFA requests to gain access to victim accounts.

attack_sequence.name: Cloud Services on Entry-point API (REST + GraphQL)
attack_sequence.description: The extracted JWT is used to authenticate directly to the Spring Boot REST/GraphQL entry API over the Azure Front Door flow.

GraphQL query depth and complexity limits
Reachable only via Front Door Private Link origin
success_indicators: Attacker successfully invokes authenticated endpoints on the entry API.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker holds a valid, unexpired Okta JWT bearer token.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: The entry API trusts the JWT issuer (Okta) and grants authorization based on the claims contained within the token.
assumptions: Token audience validation includes the targeted entry API
Attacker traffic matches expected geographic/IP patterns if conditional access is used

attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: APT29 has leveraged compromised high-privileged on-premises accounts synced to Office 365 to move laterally into a cloud environment, including through the use of Azure AD PowerShell.

attack_sequence.name: Data from Local System on Azure Blob Storage
attack_sequence.description: By exercising valid endpoints on the entry API, the attacker commands the API to fetch and return PII stored in the connected Azure Blob Storage.
blocking_controls: Private endpoint, public network access disabled
detecting_controls: Private endpoint, public network access disabled
success_indicators: Attacker reads PII data from the file store.
attack_sequence.precondition: The attacker has authenticated API access with a role or scope that permits data retrieval.
attack_sequence.exploited_condition: Blob storage implicitly trusts data retrieval commands originating from the authenticated entry API connection string.
assumptions: The compromised user's role has permissions to request sensitive blobs via the API
attack_sequence.control_note: Bypasses the private endpoint control because the request legitimately originates from the trusted internal entry_api container.
attack_sequence.procedure_excerpt: APT29 has stolen data from compromised hosts.
